#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "optparse"

verbose = false
parser = OptionParser.new do |opts|
  opts.banner = "Usage: wordcount.rb [--verbose] FILE"
  opts.on("-v", "--verbose", "Also print the number of lines") { verbose = true }
end

begin
  parser.parse!
rescue OptionParser::InvalidOption => e
  abort "#{e.message}\n#{parser.banner}"
end

abort parser.banner unless ARGV.size == 1

filename = ARGV.first

begin
  content = File.read(filename)
rescue SystemCallError => e
  abort "wordcount.rb: #{e.message}"
end

puts "Words: #{content.split.size}"
puts "Lines: #{content.lines.size}" if verbose

`wordcount.rb` is written and works as asked:

```
$ ruby wordcount.rb file.txt
Words: 5
$ ruby wordcount.rb --verbose file.txt
Words: 5
Lines: 2
```

Words are whitespace-separated tokens. I also added `-v` as a short form of `--verbose`. A missing filename, an unknown flag or an unreadable file prints a usage or error message to stderr and exits non-zero.
